title: Protected paths: destructive commands against guarded paths are refused
subject: protected-paths-guardrail
ratio: Destructive Bash commands - the remove, move, shred, truncate and shell-redirect class - against paths matching state.json protected_paths are refused by the PreToolUse guard, and every block logs a protected_path_blocked event to events.jsonl. The protected list lives at state.json protected_paths and currently reads [".harness/precedents", ".harness/precedents/*"]; the list is operator-configured and default-empty, and with an empty list the guard is a strict no-op. A blocked command is a stop-and-report condition; agents do not route around the guard.
dicta: Tier 2 on P-029, whose accepted_mutations entry records the human gate required and recorded at apply; the intake audit T-303 (audit_t303_protected_paths.md, analyst-a) was verdicted done by verifier-c (events.jsonl ts 2026-07-06T16:21:38Z). Irony carried with the row per the ledger: the one guarded path class is the registry this epic is filling. The wave-3 census item protected_paths is subsumed by this record (CD8). Frozen by the codification ledger row decision:T-377#cd-14.
scope_conditions: role:any agent issuing filesystem-destructive Bash commands in a hooked session
revisit_trigger: Revisit when the protected_paths list changes, or a destructive command against a listed path is shown passing the guard.
validity_conditions: protected_paths still lists the registry directory and its glob
